archetypes.name: caller-coverage
archetypes.rationale: The plan names four SKILL.md callers and external-reviewers.md but does not demonstrate exhaustiveness; any undiscovered consumer of gate KV output would silently break after the change.
archetypes.prompt_body: Enumerate every file in the repository that invokes degraded-tools-gate.sh or parses any of its KV outputs (DEGRADED, CODEX_STATE, CURSOR_STATE, and the new BOTH_DOWN). Compare the discovered set against the plan's explicit scope list (design/implement/research/review SKILL.md and external-reviewers.md) and flag any caller the plan omits, including hook scripts, helper scripts, or non-SKILL.md orchestrators. Also verify that the Edit-in-sync table in degraded-tools-gate.md already enumerates all four SKILL.md files and external-reviewers.md exactly as the plan claims, and surface any discrepancy between the plan's assertion and the file's actual content. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: parse-fallback
archetypes.rationale: The plan mandates that skills treat missing or non-boolean BOTH_DOWN as true (fail-safe to prompting) but does not specify the exact Bash conditional form, leaving the implementer free to pick an expression that defaults to the wrong branch.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect the plan's proposed SKILL.md gate prose — specifically the instruction 'when BOTH_DOWN is missing/not true/false, treat BOTH_DOWN=true' — and determine whether it translates unambiguously to a Bash guard that fails safe. A positive-branch check against the literal string 'true' silently auto-proceeds when BOTH_DOWN is empty or absent, the opposite of the intended fail-safe; the plan needs to specify a guard form that defaults to prompting, not proceeding. Verify that the plan's prose is precise enough to prevent an implementer from choosing the wrong branch polarity, or flag it as underspecified. Also check whether the test plan includes a case that exercises this missing-BOTH_DOWN fallback on an updated skill — confirming the fail-safe is actually tested — and flag its absence if not. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
